title: Introduce prefetch failsafe and tenant-harmonic admission to limit long-context wave erosion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several production escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers indicate repeated short-request starvation and severe tail latency during sustained waves of long-context requests. Observed behavior varies by deployment mode (hosted shows multi-tenant amplification, Dedicated shows tenant-local prefetch thrash), but root cause converges on an interaction between prefetch/quarantine logic, KV-cache eviction spikes, and an admission window that gives excessive weight to in-flight long-context batches.

Repro steps (internal):
- Synthetic mixed workload: 70% small chat requests (<=64 tokens) + 30% long-context streaming requests (>=4k tokens) at steady qps over 15m.
- Observe scheduler admission growth for long sequences, prefetch inflight counters rise, KV cache eviction rates spike, and short-request latency percentile jumps >10x.
- Added trace: prefetch tasks monopolize prefetch slots and admission reservoir for multiple host ticks, causing small-request admission suppression for ~20s windows.

Root cause hypothesis:
1) Prefetch/backfill logic uses an aggressive windowed budget that does not degrade gracefully under persistent long-context waves, leading to over-commit of admission guarantees.
2) KV-cache eviction hysteresis + prefetch bursts cause transient KV thrash, which effectively stalls short batches (loss of hot prefixes).
3) Scheduler admission weighs recent inflight sizes linearly; long sequences unfairly amplify admission score and gain disproportionate window slices.

Proposed fix (high level):
- Prefetch failsafe: introduce a per-host and per-tenant token-bucket limiter for prefetch/backfill. When the prefetch limiter is exceeded, prefetch tasks are downgraded to best-effort and their admission contribution is clipped.
- Tenant-harmonic admission: replace linear-weight admission score with harmonic-mean-based weighting that reduces the influence of very large in-flight sequences on the admission window. This gives higher relative priority to many small requests versus a few long requests.
- Eviction backoff: when eviction rates spike beyond threshold, enable short-request immortalize mode (preserve small-request prefixes for N seconds) to reduce starvation during KV thrash.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): feature-flag prefetch token-bucket on 5% of host pool in Hosted; dedicated/private customers flagged on request. Collect metrics.
- Stage 2: enable tenant-harmonic admission in canary, observe admission fairness and short-request P99.
- Stage 3: enable eviction backoff immortalize if KVEvict/sec > X for 30s.
- Full rollout gated on P99 short-request latency drop and no regression to overall throughput.

Metrics to monitor (dashboards):
- short_request_p50/p95/p99_latency_by_tenant
- admission_score_distribution_histogram
- prefetch_token_bucket_fill_rate
- kv_evictions_per_minute and kv_miss_rate
- rate of starved_batches and retry amplifications

Testing: unit + integration harness that simulates mixed-length waves and measures admission fairness and KV behaviour. Load test in CI with deterministic seeds.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- Feature flags for all three changes (prefetch limiter, harmonic admission, immortalize).
- Non-destructive by default; must be enabled per-host. Automatic fallback to previous behavior on escalation.

Links:
- Incident timeline and escalation notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/incident-long-context-wave-2025-02
- Canary run dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/prefetch-failsafe-canary
- PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1897

Why this is different: tenant-harmonic admission is a novel admission weighting designed to mathematically curb the dominance of very large sequences while still preserving throughput for bursty long-context workloads. Prefetch failsafe clips resource-hungry speculative behavior rather than attempting to tune one-size-fits-all window sizes.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after two escalations from Hosted customers and one Dedicated customer. Notified SRE and PMs. Initial triage suggests prefetch + scheduler interaction.

2025-02-13 - Marco Hernandez: Reproduced locally with mixed-length harness; confirmed KV eviction spike correlates with small-request P99 regressions. Started prototype of prefetch token-bucket limiter.
2025-02-14 - Priya Singh (SRE): Observed same pattern in Private deployment logs; recommended adding per-tenant limits as Dedicated tenants can also trigger hostwide thrash.
2025-02-15 - Design review notes from Elena Moore: Suggested immortalize window should be conservative (5-15s) and exposed as runtime knob in Console for enterprise customers.
2025-02-16 - Marco Hernandez: Implemented token-bucket prototype and a metric exporter for prefetch fill rate (PR #1897). Canary scheduled for 2025-02-18.

2025-02-18 - Canary update: 5% hosts enabled, short-request P99 decreased by 45% on canary hosts, overall token throughput unchanged. Noted one regression: a low-volume long-context benchmark saw +4% latency, acceptable for initial rollout.
2025-02-18 - QA (Anika Zhao): Added integration tests to simulate eviction spike + mixed workload; tests passing locally. Next: run chaos scenario in staging for 2h.

Action items:
- Marco: Finish tenant-harmonic admission implementation and unit tests (ETA 2025-02-20).
- Priya: Add alerts for prefetch_token_bucket_fill_rate > 80% sustained.
